words.definition:
A woman who is the head of a community of nuns.
She was a nun for many years before she became an abbess.

To cancel or do away with.
Each year, we hoped the principal would abrogate the assigning of homework.

A less common name for a cashew.
We made popcorn balls with acajou nuts.

To equip or outfit, especially a military.
The quartermaster said it was his job to make sure that they had all the supplies to fully accoutre the troops.

Referring to the main acid in vinegar.
Tasty salad oils are made with olive oil and acetic vinegar.

Bad-tempered.
When the ball flew through our window, my father spoke to my brother in an acrimonious manner.

An entertainer who performs gymnastic feats, such as walking a tightrope or swinging on a trapeze.
We saw a wonderful acrobat at the Cirque du Soleil.

Profitable, useful, or providing an advantage.
When the champion player joined the team, it was very advantageous.

Emotional support or encouragement.
The dog looked at his master for affirmation.

Trying to win in an argument.
The board member’s agonistic tone in the meeting made it hard for anyone to agree with him.

A plant in the rose family.
Some examples of an agrimony are blackberry, raspberry, and strawberry.

Plant protein found in seeds.
The seeds store aleurone as little granules in the cells.

To join or unite; to form a larger organization.
The two small towns decided to amalgamate their police forces to make it one large service.

A fine that was discretionary rather than set out in law.
In the Middle Ages, a court could impose an amercement, which could include forfeiture of goods.

A small European country.
As they were driving from France to Spain, they went through Andorra.

A condition where there is an inadequate blood supply to the heart.
The condition of angina is marked by severe pain in the chest, shoulders, and neck.

Something that departs from the normal.
In baseball, a game where one team has no hits is an anomaly.

Near the front of the body.
The veins are anterior to the heart.

Referring to suffering mental distress or uneasiness, or great fear.
She was extremely anxious about her exams.

A person who abandons a religion, political belief, or a cause.
After asking to be traded to a different team, the hockey player felt like an apostate.

A fleet of warships.
An armada of destroyers, minesweepers, and gunboats made up the invasion fleet standing just off the coast.

Harshness and roughness in manner, tone or temper.
When we kept asking the same thing over and over again, he answered with asperity.

A black, sticky substance, often mixed with small stones or sand that forms a strong surface when hard.
The new road was paved with asphalt.

Not usual.
It is atypical for every person in the class to stay home with an illness on the same day.

An extremely plain or simple, undecorated look.
My room was full of ruffles and colour while my brother liked his to be more austere.

A self-governing country or region.
Canada is a member of the British Commonwealth, but has its own autonomy.

An open declaration or an acknowledgement of a belief or intention.
A marriage vow is a type of avowal because you affirm your love and loyalty to someone.

A person’s area of expertise, authority or interest.
The student struggled with science, saying English literature was more his bailiwick.

To harass or bully.
We would not allow the opposing team to ballyrag us into losing our confidence.

Liquid clay used to decorate pottery.
The antique vase was decorated with barbotine flowers.

A fine, light fabric typically made from cotton, linen, or synthetic fibres.
The batiste dress was cool and comfortable on a hot summer day.

To thoroughly confuse.
Until I studied it carefully, geometry could really befuddle me.

Referring to being hostile, aggressive, or ready to fight or argue.
The woman took a belligerent tone when her boss questioned why she was late for work most days.

The person to whom one is engaged to be married.
In the movie, the prince and his betrothed announced their engagement at the ball.

A small, decorative ornament or trinket.
The museum’s collection of precious ornaments included a Fabergé bibelot.

Involving two parties, especially countries.
The two countries had a bilateral agreement to boost tourism.

Bad tempered and sullen.
Our new neighbour seemed to be a bilious person until we got to know him.

The study of the geographical distribution of plants and animals.
There are important biogeographic studies done to track which creatures are under threat of extinction.

The animal and plant life of a certain region, habitat or geological period.
The biologists went to the isolated island to study the biota.

Having two stages or forms.
A butterfly has a biphasic life cycle, as it changes from a crawling caterpillar into a flying insect.

A plant disease.
The Irish potato famine was caused by a blight on the potatoes.

A large meteor which explodes in the atmosphere.
A bolide is also known as a fireball.

A woodworking tool similar to a straight screwdriver.
The carpenter used a bradawl to make an indentation in the wood to ease the insertion of the screw.

Referring to a dark colour of eyes or hair.
My sister has brunette hair but I am a red-head.

An isolated hill with steep sides.
The valley was beautiful with a view of the large butte in the distance.

Projecting supports built against a wall.
We built a treehouse with a large buttress to strengthen it.

A pouch connected to the junction of the small and large intestines.
The appendix usually hangs down from the caecum.

A kind of mild white cheese.
We first tasted Caerphilly on our visit to Wales.

One of the moons of Jupiter.
The moon called Callisto is roughly four billion years old.

A small group of people who act as unofficial advisors to a person of power.
Sometimes, a camarilla is informally called a ‘kitchen cabinet’.

Musical or melodious.
Our piano teacher taught us a canorous melody for our recital.

A leap in dancing.
The ballet dancer made a spectacular capriole during the performance.

A South American mammal resembling a giant guinea pig.
The capybara is the largest living rodent.

A large North American deer related to reindeer.
Mammals like caribou can travel many miles in search of food.

The action of picking or grasping at bedclothes by a delirious person.
The carphology of the patient continued until he became fully conscious.

The main protein present in milk.
Eighty percent of the protein in milk is casein.

Historically, a form of heavily armoured cavalry fielded by ancient empires across Eurasia.
The cataphract was designed to smash through dense infantry and opposing cavalry.

A supper room, especially on an upper floor.
The literary society met for dinner in a cenacle created in historic building.

White lead used as a cosmetic face whitener in medieval times.
Because a pale complexion was an indication that the person did not have to labour outdoors, many women applied ceruse to the skin.

A species of bird in the finch family.
The chaffinch is a bird with a bluish head and dark wings.

A herb in the daisy family.
For relaxing, a cup of chamomile tea is widely enjoyed.

A thick filet of beef steak.
We ate chateaubriand at a fancy restaurant.

A sofa.
The large, overstuffed chesterfield was so comfortable that I didn’t want to get up.

The milky latex of the sapodilla tree.
The main ingredient in chewing gum is chicle.

Extremely full.
His cupboard was chockablock with toys and games.

A large, noisy insect.
The cicada is found mainly in warmer climates.

An eyelash.
A cilium fell into my eye and scratched the cornea.

An industrial city in Ohio.
While in Cincinnati, the family went to the zoo, the aquarium, and the art museum.

Often preceding a date, meaning approximately.
The house was built circa 1870.

Mercy or leniency.
The judge showed clemency by reducing the sentence.

A natural group of words that frequently appear together.
An example of a collocation is ‘make a mistake’, because we wouldn’t usually say ‘do a mistake’.

Something given to pay for a loss.
When our tree fell on the neighbour’s car, we had to pay compensation.

Willing to agree with others or obey rules.
The new restaurant ensured it was compliant with all the health department codes.

To condense or compact into less space.
By rolling it tightly, I can compress my sleeping bag so it fits easily into my pack.

A colleague or fellow member of an organization.
He looked forward to meeting up with a comrade from his days working for a political party.

The quality of having a surface that curves inwards, like the inside of a bowl.
The concavity of the mirror made us look distorted.

A large open area at the front of a public building.
The bus station has a two-storey concourse with waiting rooms and ticket booths.

The action of establishing the truth or accuracy of something.
The fans were very excited to get confirmation that the band was going on tour.

Uncertainty about what is happening, intended, or required.
There was total confusion at the airport after the snow storm caused the cancellation of many flights.

To combine a number of things into a single, unified whole.
The bank official suggested to the customer that it would be financially helpful to consolidate his outstanding debts into one loan.

A clear soup made by boiling meat, bones or vegetables.
The host started the elegant meal with a clear consommé enriched with finely diced vegetables.

Belonging to a continent.
Hudson Bay is in the Canadian part of continental North America.

A bruise.
After falling off her bike, my sister had a contusion on her knee.

To act against something in order to reduce its force.
Many initiatives, if carried out, could counteract global warming.

Extending throughout a nation.
The band used a bus to go on a countrywide tour.

Willing to believe or trust without proof.
His credulity led him to believe everything he read on social media.

A ceremonial staff carried by a bishop.
A crosier is hooked at one end like a shepherd’s crook.

To obtain ideas, services or content from a large group of people.
I used the internet to crowdsource some help assembling my new furniture.

Cross-shaped.
The knee has two cruciate ligaments, referring to the way they cross each other in an X-shape.

A ceramic or metal container used for melting metals at high heat.
The craftsman carefully poured the molten gold from the crucible into the mold.

The land and outbuildings immediately surrounding a house.
Under Canadian law, curtilage considers an attached garage to be part of the dwelling.

An ornamental strip of wood or other material with an S-shaped profile, used in architecture.
You are more likely to see a cyma on a classical house design than a modern one.

Chemical messengers that help direct an attack on a microbial invader.
The immune system may produce a variety of cytokines when fighting off germs.

To decode, solve, and explain.
He was the only one who could decipher the secret code.

A tall conical cedar tree native to the Himalayan mountains.
The deodar can grow as high as 40 to 50 metres.

To feel or express strong disapproval of something.
We deplore people who do not tell the truth.

To express disapproval of something.
The protest was held as a way to deprecate the government’s climate policy.

The action of a train or street car accidently leaving its track.
We were late getting home because of the streetcar derailment.

A crane used for lifting heavy weights.
The cargo boxes on the ship were lifted by a derrick.

Barren; uninhabited.
I enjoyed the novel about a man who was ship-wrecked on a desolate island.

The ‘two’ on dice or playing cards.
All he needed to win the card game was to draw a deuce.

The legal transfer of property from one owner to another.
The devolution of my grandfather’s farm was decided in favour of my uncles.

To say or read words aloud so that they can be written down.
I have some new spelling words to dictate to you.

To break down food into substances that can be used by the body.
Grandfather said he liked to have a nap while waiting for his body to digest his dinner.

To thwart or foil plans.
The sudden downpour served to discomfit our carefully laid plans for a picnic.

To get rid of insects, rodents, etc.
The pest control team will disinfest the old warehouse.

Not good in appearance or character.
The villain in the book was a disreputable character.

To differ in opinion, especially from the majority.
Two of the nine judges chose to dissent on the matter before them.

To gradually disappear.
The morning sun caused the thick fog to dissipate.

An amusement or pastime, especially one that acts as a distraction.
Board games provide our family with a pleasant diversion on a rainy day at the cottage.
words.pronunciation: deye-vur-zhuhn or deye-vur-shuhn or dih-vur-zhuhn or dih-vur-shuhn

words.definition:
A fleshy fruit containing a central seed or stone.
The cherry and plum are examples of a drupe.

A spiny oval tropical fruit.
Despite its terrible smell, durian is highly valued for its flavour.

A neurological disorder that causes involuntary muscle contractions and abnormal posture.
A brain injury is one of the causes of dystonia.

A long thin cake filled with cream.
For dessert, we selected an éclair topped with chocolate.

A feeling of great happiness or excitement.
When my mother baked shortbread cookies, I was in ecstasy.

A way out; exit.
We looked for an egress from the concert hall.

The omission of a sound or syllable when speaking.
Saying ‘fam-lee’ instead of ‘fam-i-lee’ is an example of an elision.

To preserve something or someone in an unaltered state.
Ancient Egyptians would embalm and mummify their kings and bury them in tombs.

A block in an artery such as a blood clot.
A pulmonary embolism needs emergency treatment.

To understand another’s feelings.
His ability to empathize made him an excellent counsellor.

Being in love or captivated by someone.
My sister’s boyfriend is completely enamoured with her.

To be caught in something, like a trap.
The whale became ensnared in fishing gear.

The difference in days between a solar year and a lunar year.
Historically, an epact was a calendar tool used to calculate the date of Easter.

A word or phrase applied to a person to describe an attributed quality.
‘Richard the Lion-Heart’ is an epithet of King Richard I.

A person or thing that is a perfect example of a certain quality or type.
The princess looked the epitome of elegance and good taste.

The quality of being fair and impartial.
The girls’ soccer team demanded equity with the boy’s team when it came to practice times.

An exercise machine that measures how much physical work your body puts out while you move.
The athletes found the rowing machine was an excellent ergometer to track their overall performance.

The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by water, winds, glaciers, etc.
The cliffs along the ocean were being worn away by erosion.

Softwood shavings used for packing fragile goods.
When we moved, mother packed her good dishes in a box filled with excelsior.

Requiring immediate action.
The exigent circumstances of the wildfire necessitated an evacuation.

A person who lives outside their native country.
The expatriate looked forward to visiting family in her homeland.
words.pronunciation: eks-pay-tree-ayt or eks-pa-tree-ayt or eks-pay-tree-iht or eks-pa-tree-iht

words.definition:
An exclamatory word or phrase, especially a swear word.
The woman accidently used an expletive when she stubbed her toe.

A person whose job is to get rid of pests from a building.
If your house has an influx of ants, call a professional exterminator.

Triumphant; jubilant.
The exultant soccer team celebrated their championship win.

To tell invented stories or create stories filled with fantasy.
The author loves to fabulate magical worlds filled with extraordinary creatures.

Easily or effortlessly done or performed.
The student’s academic achievement looked facile, but she had, in fact, worked very hard.

A voice or sound that is unusually high, especially in a man.
The singer will long be remembered for his highly emotive falsetto.

Elaborate ornaments.
Her wedding dress was covered with lace and fandangles.

Pasta in the shape of a bow or butterfly.
I love to mix my farfalle with cheese sauce.

Greatly productive; fertile.
The heavy rain turned the dry yard into a fecund garden full of green plants.

Referring to or containing iron.
Steel is a ferrous metal.

A type of kilt.
Men in Scotland wear a filibeg which show their clan’s tartan.

The thick loosely-hanging lips of a bloodhound or similar dog.
In some hounds, the flews help trap scent and direct it towards the dog’s nose as they track.

Bending, especially of a limb or joint.
It is important for the fingers to have easy and complete flexion.

An old-fashioned type of gun.
The flintlock has been replaced by more modern firearms.

A type of bronze or copper coin used by the ancient Romans.
The follis continued to be used as money as late as the sixth century.

The act of creating, shaping or arranging something.
At the glass factory, we watched the formation of a beautiful bowl.

Courage while in pain; bravery.
She endured her illness with great fortitude.

Referring to behaviour or situations that are highly active, but chaotic.
The student worked at a frenetic pace to complete the assignment on time.

An old-fashioned word meaning frozen or frosty.
The wind howled across the frore wasteland.

The fruiting of a plant, fungus, etc.
The apple tree yielded a heavy crop during fructification.

A strong fabric of cotton and flax.
The farmer wore a fustian jacket while working in the cold barn.

Ahead of the times; advanced.
The company makes futuristic computer chips.

To seize money, especially part of a person’s salary, to settle a debt or claim.
There was a court order to garnishee his wages to pay his debt.

Refined and polite.
At the formal dinner, you are expected to behave in a genteel manner.

The science of accurately measuring and understanding Earth’s geometric shape and orientation in space.
The team’s work in satellite geodesy contributed to the accuracy of modern GPS systems.

Referring to a specific genre of poetry that praises the virtues of outdoor labour and country living.
The poet said his georgic poem was to celebrate the dignity of physical toil and struggle against the elements.

An artificial human figure in Jewish folklore.
Some people believe the golem served as an inspiration for Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein.

A type of diving duck with a jagged bill.
Eating fish, nesting in holes in trees, and having a crested head are three traits of the goosander.

An expert judge of good food.
The gourmet liked to savour exotic dishes from around the globe.

A step-by-step change, or a series of stages in a progression.
The artist created a beautiful gradation of colour, smoothly blending the sunset’s fiery orange into deep purple.

A broad category of combat sports and martial arts focused on physical contact and leverage rather than striking.
The primary goal of grappling is to manipulate and unbalance an opponent.

A country in the West Indies.
The island of Grenada lies about one hundred miles off the coast of South America.

A large, nocturnal, fruit-eating bird.
The guacharo, also called an oilbird, lives in caves in Central and South America.

A two-wheeled horse-drawn cab.
The hansom accommodated two people inside, with the driver mounted on an elevated seat behind.

A dog breed used for hunting hares and rabbits.
The painting of the hunting scene featured a harrier.

Each of two or more words which are spelled identically but have different sounds and meanings, such as tear meaning ‘rip’ and tear meaning ‘liquid from the eye’.
A triple heteronym is extremely rare.

The action of sweating.
Certain foods such as hot peppers can increase hidrosis.

Went quickly.
The travellers hied back to their hotel when the downpour started.

Hairy.
Examples of hirsute plants include the staghorn sumac and the black oak.

An expert in history.
The historian worked at the National Archives.

A sandwich made of a long roll filled with meat, cheese, and salad.
Every layer of a hoagie makes it that much more flavourful.

A boisterous or carefree girl; a tomboy.
The pigtailed hoyden grew into a refined and educated woman.

Pride or arrogance.
The driver’s hubris prevented him from asking for directions, causing him to be late.

A woman who hunts.
In Roman mythology, Diana is known as the supreme huntress of the woods.

A lightly-armoured cavalry soldier, originating in 15th century Hungary, and known for their brightly-coloured uniforms.
A hussar was usually a wealthy nobleman who had to finance his own equipment.

Very small predatory animals that live in seawater.
The science student studied the hydrozoan under a microscope.

Monetary inflation occurring at a very high rate.
When prices increase very quickly, this is referred to as hyperinflation.

A person who attacks or criticizes cherished beliefs or organizations.
Because the new manager dared to question the company’s deeply held traditions, his bosses viewed him as an iconoclast.

To imagine or come up with an idea.
The department leader used brainstorming to ideate innovative options.

A picture provided in a book, newspaper, etc.
Each fairy tale in the book included a beautiful illustration.

Vastness; enormous extent.
The immensity of the Roman Empire stretched from modern-day Portugal and Britain to Iraq.

Unchanging over time; ageless.
Although I tried to change my dad’s mind, I realized his decision was immutable.

To pierce with a sharp tool.
As part of Halloween decorating, they impaled miniature pumpkins on a dead branch.

Unable to be felt by touch.
The hot dry wind brought with it clouds of impalpable dust.

To put at risk of being harmed or destroyed.
The rescue team worked tirelessly to save the imperiled hikers trapped on the mountain ledge.

Disrespectful behaviour or language; rudeness.
The teacher sent the student out of the room for his ongoing impertinence.

To have an impact, especially unwanted, on someone’s freedom, space or time.
I was being selfish and didn’t think about how my actions could impinge on others.

Silly.
The actor disliked reporters who asked inane questions.

To induct into office with formal ceremonies.
The city’s new mayor was inaugurated at a public ceremony.

Emitting light as a result of being heated.
Most homes in Canada have switched from using incandescent light bulbs to LED ones.

To provide someone with a reason to do something.
Parents sometimes incentivize their children to study more with a special treat.

A surgical cut made in skin or flesh.
Great care is taken to prevent infection when surgeons have to make an incision.

A narrow-edged tooth at the front of the mouth.
The dentist noticed a cavity on the incisor.

Not staying the same throughout.
The builder quit buying lumber from the closest store because the quality of the wood was often inconsistent.

To cause or to influence someone to accept an idea or feeling.
The teaching staff tried to inculcate their students with curiosity.

Lazy.
Nobody wants to appear indolent.

Lacking the required skill to achieve something.
Despite all efforts, the attempts to calm the restless crowd were ineffectual.

To breathe in air, gas, smoke, etc.
The family was taken to hospital after inhaling carbon monoxide.

Lacking in kindness or compassion.
The group protested the inhumane conditions of the animal shelter.

A new product, idea or method that creates value.
The use of reusable rockets was a major innovation in spaceflight technology.

An official investigation.
There was an inquiry into the cause of the fire.

Rudely or disrespectfully.
A person who speaks insolently models bad manners.

A state of being unpredictable or likely to change or fail.
Many drivers are concerned about the instability of gas prices these days.

A natural or intuitive way of acting or thinking.
The teenager’s instinct warned him to avoid the gang’s invitations.

An agreement in which you pay a company money, in the form of a premium, and they pay your costs in the event of an accident, injury, etc.
My father was glad we had good insurance when he had a car accident.

To stop or seize someone, preventing them from reaching their destination.
The police were able to intercept the suspect before he could leave the country.

Referring to an action or situation likely to arouse resentment or anger in others.
Spreading invidious gossip hurts people’s feelings.

Too powerful to be defeated or overcome.
Proud and arrogant after years of winning championship games, the team considered themselves invincible.

A type of northern Indian classical dance that tells a story.
The audience enjoyed the dazzling footwork of the Kathak dances.

A tall coniferous Australasian tree with broad leathery leaves.
Unless harvested for lumber, a kauri tree can live for a thousand years.

The basic unit of temperature.
The kelvin scale is based on absolute zero.

Art, objects, or design considered to be in poor taste.
The street vendors were selling many kitsch souvenirs.

A powder used to darken the eyelids and eyebrows.
The make-up artist applied kohl to the actress’s eyes.

The common language of the Greeks from the close of the classical period to the Byzantine era.
The priest conducted the church services in Koine.

In Judaism, referring to food that conforms to religious laws.
The restaurant in the hotel provides a special menu with certified kosher meals for guests.

A traditional southern African enclosure for livestock, such as cattle.
The kraal is surrounded by a fence or thorn bushes.

A mythical, hooved animal in Chinese mythology.
A kylin is often described as the “Chinese unicorn.”

A type of ancient Greek drinking cup.
The museum curator carefully placed the kylix in a glass display case.

A sailor from the East Indies.
The lascar helped manage the rigging as the ship entered the harbour.

A reading from scripture in liturgy.
The church member read the lection each Sunday.

A furnace used for the gradual heating and cooling of glass.
They used the lehr to cool the glass slowly.

Characterized by mercy or tolerance.
The judge was lenient and only gave the first-time offender a stiff fine.

A dense white scar or spot on the cornea of the eye caused by injury or infection.
The deep eye injury healed, but left a permanent leucoma that blurred his vision.

Relating to the words or vocabulary of a language.
A dictionary is a lexical reference.

Freedom.
Rules and laws exist to keep us safe and ensure everyone’s right to liberty is protected.

Not forbidden; lawful.
My grandmother has licit permission to park in designated accessible spots.

A soft coal.
The lignite is a greater polluter than the hard bituminous coal.

An old stringed instrument like a small U-shaped harp.
The musician plucked the strings of the lyre to accompany the ancient song.

A full-length waterproof coat made of rubberized cloth.
The British author described his detective as wearing a mackintosh.

A periodical publication containing articles and illustrations.
The landscaper was thrilled to have her articles published in a gardening magazine.

Instrument for measuring a magnetic field.
Archaeologists and geological investigators use magnetometers.

Electron tubes for generating microwaves.
Today, magnetrons are used in radar and in microwave ovens.

The action of taking care of something.
The old car needed a lot of maintenance.

To speak about someone in a maliciously critical way.
The mean-spirited gossips would not have dared to malign her if her friend had been present.

Suffering from a lack of proper nutrition.
Many children in the refugee camp were malnourished.

A tropical tree having edible fruit with sweet yellow flesh.
The mammee is native to tropical areas of the Americas.

An excessive enthusiasm or excitement.
The car collector’s mania for automobiles led him to rent out a warehouse for a garage.

Mass-produced, relatively inexpensive goods marketed as luxurious or prestigious.
The masstige skincare line gave the feeling of luxury at a drug store price.

The moving or mechanical part of something.
The child was fascinated to see the mechanism of the clock.

The combining of two things, especially companies, into one.
Consumers hoped the merger between the two supermarket chains would not result in higher prices.

In botany, a small opening in the surface of an ovule through which the pollen tube penetrates.
The micropyle is often visible as a small pore in the ripe seed.

A substance used to kill mites.
Carefully read the label on the miticide to make sure it is safe to use in the planned setting.

Warning or admonishing.
The mother shook a monitory finger at her son to stop him from touching the hot stove,

A small mountain or hill.
The hiking trail took them up the monticule and down the other side.

Relating to the scientific study of the form or structure of plants and animals.
Scientists study the morphological differences between fish fins and bird wings to better understand evolution.

Very generous.
She received a piano for her birthday from her munificent aunt.

A large group of starlings.
The murmuration flew together in highly coordinated patterns.

Relating to the muscles.
The heart is a muscular organ, divided into left and right sides.

The science of organizing and managing museums.
The anthropology student took several courses in museology.

Relating to the muscular tissue of the heart.
The doctor said the patient had suffered a myocardial infarction, also known as a heart attack.

A sleep disorder.
Her uncle would fall asleep at any moment due to narcolepsy.

The death of body cells or tissues of a plant or animal.
The plant leaves showed signs of necrosis after being damaged by the frost.

To make ineffective, nullify.
Shipping charges can negate the money saved by buying something online.

Discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
The negotiation was long and tense before a solution was reached.

A poison that attacks the nervous system.
Examples of a neurotoxin are the venom of a rattlesnake or black widow spider.

An unproven, and likely ineffective, medication.
A quick search on line will find many a nostrum promising to cure cancer and other serious illnesses.

Harmful, poisonous, or very unpleasant.
The homeowner called the city to report the noxious smell coming from the sewer.

To help or encourage someone during a period of training or development.
The nursery school promised to nurture young children.

An antibiotic used to treat fungal infections.
The doctor prescribed nystatin drops when the toddler developed thrush, an infection of the mouth.

In botany, a dry cover or casing around a stem.
The buckwheat plant has an ocrea around the stem.

Another term for the hashtag or pound sign.
The octothorp was adopted by printers in the 19th century as a ‘number sign’.

An instrument for measuring distance travelled by a vehicle.
When buying a used car, it is crucial to check the odometer.

Having or giving off a smell or scent.
We explored a dark and odorous cave.

An S-shaped curve used in building design and art.
We were told that the arch above the door of the old church is a fine example of an ogee.

A print textured to resemble an oil painting.
She bought a Miro oleograph, which people mistook for an original.

Relating to or characteristic of an opera.
The soprano constantly practiced operatic arias.

A small African antelope with short vertical horns.
The tiny oribi is about the size of a greyhound dog.

The small bones of the inner ear.
The otoliths can sense gravity and movement.

A state of nervous excitement or anxiety.
When the family’s dog went missing, they were overwrought.

A word or name with an acute accent on the last syllable.
The Frenchman explained that his name was an oxytone.

The ocean between the Americas to the east and Asia and Australia to the west.
The Pacific is the largest and deepest of all the oceans.

A person who writes short, unbound booklets.
